mcts._eval_simulations_note: 600, matching num_simulations. v7 trained at 600 and evaluated at 200, so the accept gate, the racing-decay tripwire and the greedy_min_seat floor all judged an agent that self-play was not producing — a different search depth is a different player, not a cheaper measurement of the same one. EXPECT THE GREEDY NUMBER TO FALL, not rise: re-scoring n2_9x9_v7 iteration 60 at K=16 gives 70.0% vs greedy at 200 sims and 55.0% at 600 (seat 1 4/10 vs 1/10; seat 0 is 10/10 either way). More search makes this model worse against a racer, which is itself the finding — it is not a reason to keep measuring at the wrong budget. Affordable because eval_games drops 160 -> 40: 40 x 600 = 24,000 sim-units against v7's 160 x 200 = 32,000.
mcts._dirichlet_alpha_note: 0.3, raised from 0.1 to record what actually ran. Neither this key nor c_puct ever reached the search: _mcts() and the self-play workers built MCTSConfig with only num_simulations, dirichlet_epsilon, max_rollout_depth and wall_candidates, and TrainingConfigMP had no field for either, so every run through v7 used MCTSConfig's defaults — alpha 0.3, c_puct 1.41. Both are wired now, and the value here is set to what was effective so wiring them changes no behaviour and v8 stays attributable to the aliasing fix and the live gate. c_puct is unchanged because config and default already agreed. Tuning alpha is a deliberate future experiment, not a side effect of this fix.
mcts._num_simulations_note: 600. The visits-per-action argument for 1200 (140 actions / 600 sims = 4.3 visits) assumed a prior spread uniformly over 128 wall actions — wall_mask_iters removes that premise, since the masked phase has ~4 legal actions and the unmasked phase starts from a move-concentrated prior. Self-play is 93% of the iteration, so 600 roughly halves the run: N=2 ~32h vs ~62h at 150 iters.

training._iters_note: num_iterations/games_per_iteration are per variant; N=4 games run ~3x longer so it buys fewer of them for the same wall clock
training._replay_buffer_note: 100k ~= 7 iterations of coverage at N=2 — the regime runs/n2_5x5_buf10k_v1 validated.
training._ply_counted_note: max_game_moves and explore_moves both count plies, not rounds — set per variant so each player gets the same budget; see variants.n2/n4
training._gate_arm_note: The vs-best gate is HELD until win_vs_greedy exceeds gate_arm_greedy_min, then the champion is seeded from that checkpoint. v7 never accepted (untrained champion = wall-spammer, gate games never decided, 41% of wall time). v8 armed correctly (N=2 at iter 4, 73.8%) and STILL never accepted: two trained wall-capable models stall each other past max_game_moves 160 (32-38 of 40 gate games timed out, decided floor 10/40 unreachable at any strength) — hence gate_max_game_moves. The min is 0.05 because v8's N=4 armed on a single 1/80 win and seeded a champion that was not a racer.
training._discount_unit_note: Per-variant: 'round' decays per the mover's own turns, 'ply' per move by anybody. Measured better at N=2, worse at N=4.
training._accept_margin_note: 0.14 at eval_games=40. Sigma depends on DECIDED games, not eval_games, and the margin has to be recalibrated whenever eval_games moves or the gate silently changes strictness. History: 0.05 at 80 games was +0.9 sigma = 19% false accepts and v4's post-iter-15 accepts were consistent with pure noise; 0.08 at 160 games was +1.79 sigma at the ~78% decided rate those runs saw. At 40 games, 0.08 would be +1.01 sigma — back to the defect. The gate is now armed only once the learner beats greedy (gate_arm_on_greedy), so the champion is a racer that reaches its goal and games decide at roughly 100% rather than 78%: 40 games ~= 40 decided, sigma 0.079, and 0.14 is +1.77 sigma — the same strictness as 0.08@160, at a quarter of the cost.
training._wall_mask_note: wall_mask_fraction, NOT the phase/ramp (both now 0). Measured against probe_n2_ramp/best.pt: get_valid_actions gates walls on walls_remaining>0, so budget 1 and budget 10 are the SAME 131-action problem (3 legal at budget 0). Every ramp step above 0 was a no-op and the whole cliff is 0 -> 1. The collapse is value-coverage loss, not prior dilution: after a fully masked phase the value head has never seen a walled state, while root Dirichlet noise (eps 0.25 over 131 actions) inflates wall prior mass 0.00024 -> 0.245 (NOTE: this was computed for alpha 0.1, which never reached the search -- 0.3 was effective; the 0.245 figure is driven by eps and the action count, not by alpha, so it stands. It does predate mcts_wall_candidates, which cuts the noise support from 131 to ~19), so ~24% of self-play moves become near-random walls that MCTS cannot reject. 0.5 mixes wall-free and full-wall games in EVERY iteration from the first, so neither distribution is ever out of coverage. MEASURED (n2_9x9_v6, n4_9x9_v6): it cures the collapse and nothing else. No relapse on any signal -- avg_len flat 25-34, draws <=12%, loss_p monotone down, self-play holds the racing seat split P1=25-30/40 -- and win_vs_greedy is still 0.000 at every eval, 0/600 decided games, EVERY seat 0/20, including N=2 seat 1 where the fully masked probe got 18/20 at iteration 4. So the mix is worse at producing a racer than the phase it replaced, and coverage was never the constraint on strength. Do not raise or lower this expecting strength; the racer has to come from the opponent pool (opponent_greedy_share). See academic_experiences.md 8.6.
training._reward_decay_note: 0.99, NOT 0.97. Probed both 5x5 arms vs greedy at tensor spec v1, 20 games/seat: gamma=0.99 goes 40/40 (seat 0 with exactly 1 wall/game), gamma=0.97 goes 20/40, losing seat 0 entirely (0/20) by over-walling at 3/game. Seat 0 is won only by spending a turn on a wall that pays off later, and a steeper discount makes that lose to advancing now. The 2026-06 gamma ablation measured loss_v drift only and says nothing about playing strength.
training._greedy_stop_note: Abort on racing decay, which the gate cannot see: in local_9x9_v6 it accepted at 69% and 60% while greedy fell 60% -> 10% over the same window. One seat is always winnable by racing alone (seat 1 at N=2, seat 0 at N=4), so the best per-seat rate has a hard ceiling and only falls if the policy stops racing. Warns on the first eval 20+ pts below the peak, stops on the second. best.pt holds the peak, so an early stop still ships the good model.
training._greedy_stop_z_note: A strike needs the drop to clear BOTH greedy_stop_drop and greedy_stop_z sigma. Without the sigma test a model whose true rate never changes aborts 53-92% of the time, because the peak is a max over seats and evals (see academic_experiences.md 8.5). At 20 games/seat only a collapse is detectable; that is what racing decay looks like.
training._greedy_min_seat_note: Companion to the decay watch, which can only fire on a fall from a peak. probe_n4_ramp peaked at 0.10 against a 0.20 drop, so a strike was arithmetically impossible and it ran 10 h past the point the answer was known. 0.25 is a deliberately low bar: after the masked phase the model should own the seat racing wins. Armed only once the mask ends, since every run is below it while untrained.
training._minimax_note: The HELD-OUT baseline. Once the opponent pool anchors on greedy, win_vs_greedy measures fit rather than generalisation, and nothing else is held out: vs_random saturates at 100% by iteration 5 and the gate is relative to a moving champion. minimax is depth-limited maxn on MovesToFinish(nearest rival) - MovesToFinish(self), the conventional Quoridor baseline, and unlike greedy it PLACES WALLS -- measured 11 wins in 12 games against greedy at 9x9 N=2 with 6.3 walls/game. Wall candidates are restricted to slots touching some player's shortest path, which is what makes depth 2 affordable: ~19 s per 40-game eval at both player counts.
training._mcts_wall_candidates_note: Expand only pawn moves + the walls that cut some player's shortest path. 9x9 offers 131 legal actions at the opening, so 600 sims buy 4.6 visits each and the visit histogram cannot move away from the prior that seeded it -- 5x5 gets 17.1 and plays optimally. 16 gives 19 searched actions = 31.6 visits/action at 600, 63 at 1200. A wall missing every shortest path cannot change any distance to goal, so this is an exact filter, not a heuristic; _path_blockers already computes it for wall legality, costing ~10%. Search only: the rules, the env and the 140-wide policy head are untouched. Reproduce with scripts/bench_search_actions.py.
training._mcts_wall_candidates_comparability: COMPARABILITY: a result scored at K != 0 is not comparable to one scored without it, and the gap depends on whether the checkpoint TRAINED under it. n2_9x9_v7 (trained K=16) scores 80.0% vs greedy at K=16 and 47.5% at K=0, almost all of it seat 1 (12/20 -> 1/20); probe_n2_ramp (trained K=0) is flat, 35.0% -> 37.5%. So this is train/test consistency, not free strength for an arbitrary checkpoint -- always score a checkpoint at the K it trained under, on its own tensor spec, and never put pre- and post-restriction numbers in one table without a K column. See docs/restricted_wall_search.md.
training._anchored_sample_share_note: Target share of each training BATCH drawn from anchored games. opponent_greedy_share governs how many anchored games are PRODUCED; this governs how much gradient they get, and the two diverge by ~9x at N=2 and ~20x at N=4 because the model holds one seat and a scripted racer ends the game sooner. Left uniform, 35% of games became ~10% of the gradient in runs/n2_9x9_anchored: enough to acquire racing by iteration 8 (seat 1 17/20) and not enough to still have it at iteration 12 (0/20), with the racing-decay tripwire firing correctly. 0.3 is the first setting that makes the anchored signal a real minority rather than a rounding error.
training._greedy_min_seat_after_note: The floor arms at max(wall_mask_iters, this). A mixed run sets wall_mask_iters=0, so without this the floor would arm at iteration 0 and — at eval_every 4, patience 2 — could abort a healthy run at iteration 8 before it has trained. 12 gives three evals of grace.
training._eval_every_note: 4, not 5: probe_n2_ramp peaked at iteration 4 (45% vs greedy, seat 1 18/20) and the gate must land ON it to put it in best.pt. The peak is early; missing it costs the deliverable.
training._gate_max_game_moves_note: vs-best eval only; self-play and the other evals keep max_game_moves. 320 = 2x the N=2 cap. Costs time only on games that would otherwise time out at 160 anyway.
training._anchored_seat0_note: Fraction of anchored games pinned to seat 0 (rest rotate over 1..N-1). At N=4 greedy-vs-greedy is 60/60 for seat 0, so it is the ONLY seat a racer can win and the pooled ceiling is 25%; under uniform rotation seat 0 was ~300 of ~8400 samples/iter (v8 measured) because its games are also the shortest. 0 at N=2: both seats are winnable there and rotation already splits them evenly.
training._init_checkpoint_note: Warm-start weights for a FRESH run (ignored on resume), produced by scripts/pretrain_greedy.py. Attacks the opening prior directly: 128 of 131 legal opening actions are walls, so an untrained net is a wall-spammer and six N=4 attempts (v5-v8) never acquired racing from RL alone. Empty = cold start.

parallel._num_workers_note: Match the pod's cgroup cpu quota (16). Above it the jupyter server stops answering its own health check, whose entrypoint runs pkill -9 on failure.

n2._num_workers_note: 8, not the parallel section's 16, because n2 and n4 run CONCURRENTLY: 8 + 8 matches the 16-cpu cgroup quota exactly. Above the quota the jupyter server stops answering its own health check and the entrypoint pkills the run. Raise to 16 if running this variant alone.
n2._opponent_greedy_share_note: Share of GAMES anchored against the scripted racer. The gradient follows SAMPLES, not games: the model holds 1 of 2 seats and a racer ends the game sooner, so 35% of games was ~10-12% of samples in runs/n2_9x9_anchored. Tune against samples_by_source in the history row, never opponent_mix. Anchoring is what took seat 1 from 0/20 to 17/20 by iteration 8 where the mixed curriculum alone was 0/600 through iteration 20.
n2._sizing_note: 160 x 60 = 9,600 self-play games, raised from 40 x 60 = 2,400. The 2,400 figure is what n2_9x9_v7 ran, and it is a TENTH of n2_9x9_v4's 160 x 150 = 24,000. Scoring the two against each other at that gap measures budget, not method: v4 also had a live gate (15 accepts over 30 evals, shipping best.pt from iteration 145) while v7's gate never fired once, so v7 shipped an unselected iteration 60. 9,600 plus the repaired gate removes the selection confound outright and most of the budget one — a v8 win over v4 is then decisive, and a v8 loss is still arguable on budget. Full v4 parity would be ~4 days of wall clock. The racing-decay and never-acquired stops still end a failing run early, so 60 iterations is a ceiling, not a plan.

n4._games_per_iteration_note: 160, raised from 40 alongside n2. At N=4 this is also what gives the seat-0 anchored signal enough gradient to measure: the model holds 1 of 4 seats, so 40 games/iter anchored seat 0 in only 6 games per iteration (3 walled, 3 wall-free) once the aliasing fix rotates seats evenly. 160 makes it ~24. Seat 0 is the only seat a racer can win at N=4 and it finishes in ~6.2 moves, so it yields far fewer SAMPLES per game than the later seats — the game count has to be generous for the sample count to be adequate. The greedy_min_seat tripwire still caps a failing run at ~20 iterations.
n4._opponent_greedy_share_note: 0.5, higher than n2's 0.35: the model holds only 1 of 4 seats, so an anchored game yields roughly a quarter of the samples a self-play game does (measured 20x with an untrained net, narrowing as racing improves). N=4 also needs it most -- self-play among four identical agents rewards camping for jumps, which is close to the opposite of the seat-0 racing the evaluation scores.
n4._eval_greedy_note: 80, not 40: the greedy eval rotates the candidate through all N seats, so at N=4 a 40-game eval is only 10 games per seat — and greedy_stop_patience keys on the BEST per-seat rate, which at n=10 has SE ~0.095, making the 20-pt abort threshold barely 2 sigma. 80 gives 20/seat, matching n2, where 20-pt is ~4 sigma. Costs ~20s an eval against a ~500s iteration.
n4._sizing_note: 40 x 40, smaller than n2's 60 x 80 because N=4 games run to a 320-ply cap and cost roughly twice as much per game. Both earlier N=4 probes used the phase/ramp curriculum now known to be inert, so the mixed curriculum is untried here — this run is a real test, not a repeat. The racing-decay and never-acquired stops bound it.
